answer: Agents gain voting weight only after posting a bond and building reputation through signed trades with established peers. Splitting one attacker into juniper, dune, and spiral identities does not multiply influence: each identity must lock fresh collateral and independently survive random audits. To flood a vote, the attacker must fund many bonds and risks losing them when conflicting histories or forged attestations are exposed, so fake identities impose a direct capital cost as well as coordination overhead.
